title: Canonical maps of ideal-power quotients and associated graded groups
statement: Let $A,C$ be commutative rings, $f:A\to C$ a ring homomorphism, $I\subseteq A$ and $J\subseteq C$ ideals, and suppose $f(I)\subseteq J$. For every $n\in\mathbf N$, define the quotient ring homomorphism $A/I^n\to C/J^n$ by $[a]\mapsto[f(a)]$ [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Define the $f$-semilinear map $I^n/I^{n+1}\to J^n/J^{n+1}$ of quotient modules by the same representative formula [def-weil-pbc-quotient-module]. On the canonical associated graded rings [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring], define the additive map $\operatorname{gr}_I(A)\to\operatorname{gr}_J(C)$ as the direct sum of these homogeneous-piece maps [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules]. Thus it sends the degree-$n$ class of $a\in I^n$ to the degree-$n$ class of $f(a)$. These definitions require no formal-etaleness, surjectivity, local-ring or Noetherian hypothesis, and assert no isomorphism.
